My constructor-agnostic scan over every *.py under tests/ finds no other instance, so the release-flow family is genuinely closed, but 'the family is closed' unqualified is the third statement of the sentence that was already wrong twice.

the follow_ons characterisation is wrong for one of the three: the manifest says all three factories 'hardcode gate_results=[] internally', but _stub_exporter here returns SimpleNamespace(exported_count=len(review_batch), all_gates_passed=all_gates_passed) at :99 with no gate_results attribute at all. two proofs the brief made explicit are not in the manifest. A later node reopening the aperture question after this worktree's /dev/shm is cleared has no command to re-run and must re-derive the search, which the brief names as the documented cause of the two prior false closures.

the docstring says the report is 'shaped exactly as _record_export_accounting reads it', but that consumer at catalog_release.py:1696-1709 reads only total_candidates, exported_count, exclusion_counts and exclusion_records; neither new parameter is read on this path, because run_review_release returns at :1990 inside the if dry_run: at :1964, before the verdict read at :2008. A reader adding a case here who trusts the docstring will write all_gates_passed=False expecting the rehearsal outcome to change, and it cannot. The uniform discipline is defensible; the sentence claiming the consumer reads these fields is not.

raw_text:
ANSWER ONE - is the search right. Re-derived independently rather than read. My instrument: an AST scan over every *.py under tests/ (not only test_*.py, so conftest factories are in aperture), constructor-agnostic (any call carrying an exported_count keyword, so ExportReport, Mock and SimpleNamespace alike), covering module-level functions and fixtures, classifying all_gates_passed and gate_results as from-param, LITERAL or ABSENT, plus every exporter= keyword argument and every export-related monkeypatch.setattr in the tree. Run at 497462fec and at the integrated head. The diff is exactly the four named factories moving from LITERAL or ABSENT to from-param on both fields, and nothing else moves. So for the release flow the node's result is RIGHT and I confirm it with a wider instrument. The claim as worded is over-broad: tests/standard_names/test_cli_export.py:24 and :46 are module-level factories with hardcoded verdicts and no verdict parameter, 16 call sites, and the node's classifier is structurally unable to see them because it keys on SimpleNamespace( while these build real ExportReport objects. They feed run_export for CLI-output tests and never reach run_review_release, so they are the same shape outside the family, not a fifth member of it. What is missing is the boundary, and an unstated boundary is what produced the two prior false closures.
ANSWER TWO - the three residual factories. Verified, with one correction. test_review_release.py:55 and test_exclusion_report_is_reachable.py:92 do take the verdict and do hardcode gate_results=[]. test_release_rehearsal_writes_nothing.py:92 does NOT hardcode []; it omits gate_results entirely (:99). Same defect in kind, one level down: a value the double supplies on the test's behalf. Different in consequence: catalog_release.py:2016 reads gate_results only when the verdict is False and :2017-2020 falls back to () on AttributeError, so both [] and absent land on the :2028 refusal 'names no failed export gates' rather than the :2033 named-gate refusal. The original defect let a test inherit an unstated outcome; this one lets a test state a refusal it cannot substantiate. LATENT, not reachable: every call site of all three passes all_gates_passed=True (22 sites in test_review_release.py, 2 via _run_cut at :188 and :260, 1 at :148), so the is False branch never runs and gate_results is never read; the writes_nothing site additionally runs dry_run=True and asserts at :158 that the leg never ran at all.
ANSWER THREE - the declined sites. CONFIRMED. The coordinator's instruction was conditional - remove them if they are stale comments describing a double that now requires its verdict. At test_review_release.py:478 and :655 each comment sits above a closure defined inside a single test function, and each closure still returns all_gates_passed=True, gate_results=[] hardcoded, so the comment accurately describes its double and the condition is unmet. Removing it would leave an undescribed hardcoded double, which is worse than leaving it. The node's reading and its refusal are both right. One wording slip: the manifest cites lines 471 and 640, which are the closure headers; the comments are at 478 and 655.
ANSWER FOUR - the equality and the value. Equality holds at the integrated head: 2, 2, 3, 5 per file, exit 0 each, 12 passed combined; base 497462fec extracted and run gives the same 2, 2, 3, 5. The value check the fence asks for: checkout, body_authored and preview_link hardcoded True and [] at base and every head call site passes exactly True and [], so no site's value moved. One value did move - the rehearsal _export_report carried NEITHER attribute at base and returns True and [] at head - and it cannot be a converted refusal, because run_review_release returns at catalog_release.py:1990 inside the if dry_run: at :1964, before the verdict read at :2008, and the rehearsal's only consumer _record_export_accounting reads solely total_candidates, exported_count, exclusion_counts and exclusion_records. The base suite passing with the verdict absent is itself the proof that path is unreached, since :2008-2014 refuses a missing verdict and test_release_gate_verdict_is_read.py:89 shows that refusal firing. No site previously exercised a refusal and now reads True.
DETECTOR - the figure the manifest omits: grep -rn 'Export gates are scaffolding' tests/ returns 5 sites in 4 files at 497462fec and 2 sites in 1 file at head, both survivors being the declined closures at test_review_release.py:478 and :655.
